pharm: Anti-inflammatory/analgesic; prodrug largely metabolised to diclofenac; preferential effect on inflamed tissue
quick: Caution; avoid if severe; monitor LFTs
summary: Aceclofenac is a phenylacetic acid NSAID and a prodrug largely metabolised to diclofenac, with anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects preferentially in inflamed tissue. It is used for pain and inflammation in osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis at 100 mg twice daily. It shares the class GI, cardiovascular, renal and hepatic risks of NSAIDs and is contraindicated in active GI bleeding, severe organ impairment, established cardiovascular disease and the third trimester of pregnancy. It is not FDA-approved but is used in Europe and Asia.
indications: Pain and inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis
Pain and inflammation in ankylosing spondylitis
admin: Swallow tablets whole with a glass of water
Do not crush or chew sustained-release tablets
Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration
moa: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis; largely metabolised to diclofenac, producing anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic effects with a preferential action on inflamed tissue.

absolute: Active or recurrent peptic ulcer or GI bleeding
Established cardiovascular disease (IHD, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease)
relative: Mild to moderate cardiac, renal or hepatic impairment

preg: Contraindicated in the third trimester (risk of ductus arteriosus closure and oligohydramnios); avoid in the first and second trimesters unless essential.
lact: No data on excretion in breast milk; not recommended during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution; contraindicated in severe renal impairment. Monitor renal function, especially with diuretics, ACE inhibitors or ARBs.
hepatic: Use with caution; contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment. Monitor liver function tests.

major: Other NSAIDs or aspirin - increased GI toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors/ARBs/diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and renal injury
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate liver function tests and affect renal function tests

counsel: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
Report black stools, abdominal pain, chest pain or jaundice
Do not use in late pregnancy
Use caution if you have hypertension, cardiac or renal disease
pk: Below 25-30 C, protect from moisture and light
pearls: Prodrug largely converted to diclofenac, sharing its CV, GI and hepatic risk profile
Claimed better GI tolerability and chondroprotection, but evidence is limited
Not FDA-approved; used in Europe and Asia
missed: Take when remembered unless it is near the next dose, then skip; do not double the dose.
overdose: Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, dizziness, drowsiness and headache, with possible GI bleeding, acute kidney injury, hepatic dysfunction and rarely seizures. Management is supportive with activated charcoal within 1 hour and monitoring of renal and hepatic function; there is no specific antidote and dialysis is not useful due to high protein binding.
